ledger.claim: The threshold test under POL-RD-01 is governed by the trace figure, and the trace says this trip was driven 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 8.2 km. The derived excess is 2.98 km, or 36.34% of optimal, so both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate are passed (more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal) and a route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own telemetry. I rely on gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 11.18 km, not on trip_record.actual_distance_km of 11.2 km, as POL-RD-01 requires.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00103 and agree on the trip's timing, the trace running from 08:07:20 to 08:36:20 on 14 July 2026 against a trip_record that starts at 08:07:20 and ends at 08:36:20. The three artifacts describe the same trip.

The trace is clean for policy purposes and no escalation under POL-RD-10(3) is available to the driver: coverage is 100%, there are 175 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval against an expected interval of 10 seconds, the gaps array is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so no independent corroboration is required and the trace may be used directly.

The rider does not need corroboration beyond the trace to bring this claim: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 rider-profile sub-limb (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not engage and no extra independent source is required for an excess of this size.

The diversion itself is genuine and the rider does not contest the driver's side of the distance-and-time question: LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260714-031 closes Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd from 05:30 to 12:00, that is the very arterial the routing engine's stored optimal route uses, and the advisory's window overlaps the trip window. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met, so the measured excess is exonerated on distance and time. That exoneration is, however, the predicate for the pass-through correction claimed below, not a reason to leave the rider paying the CTE gantries.

Because the deviation is exonerated as an EXTERNAL EVENT under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) applies on its own terms: the distance and time charges stand, but the off-route ERP charges are still refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at SGD 12.00 per trip. The off-route ERP actually charged is $4.00, so the full $4.00 is due and the cap is nowhere near binding. The rider did not cause the closure and should not bear its gantry cost.

Both charged gantries are on the record as off the optimal route: CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at $1.00 each carry on_optimal_route false, and the trip_record's optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, matching the rider's account that the route she booked carries no gantry at all. The whole $4.00 was incurred solely by the CTE diversion and none of it is a charge the optimal route would have attracted.

The driver cannot convert this into a rider-caused detour and so cannot shut off the ERP correction through POL-RD-09(3). POL-RD-04(a) requires the instruction to come from the rider; the only message naming a route came from the DRIVER ('braddell close today, i take CTE ah', sent 08:12:30), and the rider's single reply 'ok' at 08:12:58 is a bare acknowledgement of a decision the driver had already announced, not an instruction identifying a place or road to act on, with waypoint_hint null on the record. POL-RD-04 is unavailable, and the pass-through refund under POL-RD-09(2) remains payable.

On the fare breakdown's own closure arithmetic the correction is at least as large: running the POL-RD-02 recomputation against the closure-adjusted optimal of 11.18 km and 28.6 minutes gives a recomputed fare of $20.993 against a charged total of $25.12, a differential of $4.127, which rounds UP to $4.15 under the fare_model rounding rule. If the tribunal takes that route rather than the POL-RD-09(2) standalone correction, the amount payable is $4.15; and under POL-RD-09(1) the $4.00 of ERP is in that case already comprehended inside the figure and must not be added on top of it. The two routes to the correction are alternatives, not cumulative.

The driver's diversion is exonerated under POL-RD-03 on this trip's own record. LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260714-031 closes Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd from 05:30 to 12:00 on 14 July 2026, and the platform's routing engine confirms this is the arterial the booked optimal route traverses ('optimal is Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials'). The advisory window overlaps the trip (08:07-08:36), the fare_breakdown closure block records intersects_route true and overlaps_trip_window true, and the driver's trace leaves the optimal corridor at the Lorong 1 Toa Payoh slip, inside the advisory geometry, before rejoining it. This is not the uncited 'traffic was bad' assertion that POL-RD-08 discards: the driver points to a specific traffic_advisory ID that covers the trip window, and the rider acknowledged the diversion in the chat log ('ok' at 08:12:58).

Exoneration under POL-RD-03 is complete, not partial. The cap on justified excess is 130% of the alternative's additional distance over the booked optimal (10.6 - 8.2 = 2.4 km) plus 1.0 km tolerance, i.e. 4.12 km. The measured excess is 2.98 km, below the cap, so the whole of it is justified. The closure-adjusted optimal distance is 8.2 + 2.98 = 11.18 km, exactly the trace distance of 11.18 km recorded by the GPS trace, so after adjustment there is no excess left for POL-RD-02 to reach.

Because POL-RD-03 fully excuses the deviation, POL-RD-02 has no unexcused excess to recompute against and the distance and time charges stand. The fare_breakdown's own closure-adjusted recomputation confirms it: against the closure-adjusted optimal (11.18 km / 28.6 min) the recomputed fare is 20.993 against a charged total of 25.12, and that gap is dominated by the $4.00 of off-route ERP rather than by any unjustified distance or time. The $8.50 figure appearing against the unadjusted 8.2 km optimal is not the correct measure once the closure is taken into account.

The deviation is not a MATERIAL deviation, so POL-RD-06's pattern check and FULL_REFUND uplift are not engaged. The excess is 36.34%, below the 50% material threshold, and 2.98 km, below the 8.0 km material threshold, and materiality is assessed on the excess remaining after POL-RD-03, which is zero. In any event the driver_profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 553 completed_trips_90d, far below the POL-RD-06 pattern threshold, so there is no repeat-deviation pattern, no basis for the FULL_REFUND uplift and no basis for a conduct referral.

There is no billing-integrity failure in the ERP lines. Both CTE gantries are matched to the driver's own trace: the erp_gantry_proximity block places a fix 0.0 m from the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry at 08:12:50 and 40.25 m from the CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) gantry at 08:19:40, both well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 uses. The two charges are genuine crossings, so POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged and no phantom-line referral is warranted against the driver.

The most the policy moves on this record is the off-route ERP pass-through, and nothing more. Where POL-RD-03 exonerates the deviation, POL-RD-09(2) returns off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone correction capped at SGD 12.00; the off-route ERP here totals SGD 4.00 (both gantry lines carry on_optimal_route false), which is below the cap. That is the same $4.00 the rider asks for and it is the ceiling: no distance or time charge is disturbed, because the closure-adjusted optimal matches what the driver drove, and no POL-RD-02 refund is added on top of it.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the shape of this trip, and the record supports it. The booked optimal route (Bishan to Kallang Wave Mall, via Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd) was 8.2 km and carried no ERP at all. The driver actually drove 11.18 km - the GPS trace figure, which governs over the 11.2 km rounded copy on the trip record - an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.34%. That passes both limbs of POL-RD-01, so a route deviation is established.

The deviation itself is excused, and the rider has accepted this. LTA advisory ADV-20260714-031 closed Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd from 05:30 to 12:00 on 14 July 2026 - the very arterial the stored optimal route uses - and the driver's trace leaves the corridor at the Lorong 1 Toa Payoh slip inside the closure geometry and rejoins it afterwards. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met. The justified excess is capped at 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km; the measured excess of 2.98 km sits below that cap, so the whole of it is excused. The closure-adjusted optimal is 11.18 km / 28.6 min, nothing remains for a distance-or-time refund, and the distance and time charges stand.

What the driver cannot pass on to the rider is the ERP. Both charged gantries - CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at $1.00 - are recorded as off the optimal route, and the booked optimal route would have attracted $0.00 of ERP. Under POL-RD-09(2), where a deviation is excused as an external event under POL-RD-03, the off-route ERP is refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00 per trip. The off-route ERP is $3.00 + $1.00 = $4.00, below the cap, so the full $4.00 is returned. That is the amount of the partial refund.

The rider's alternative computation of $4.15 is not adopted. That figure comes from running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal (charged total $25.12 less a recomputed $20.993). POL-RD-02 runs only where no exculpatory clause fully excuses the deviation; here POL-RD-03 fully excuses it, so POL-RD-02 has nothing to recompute and the distance and time charges stand. POL-RD-09(1) would in any event forbid adding the $4.00 of ERP on top of a POL-RD-02 figure. The two paths to a correction are alternatives, and on these facts the ERP pass-through under POL-RD-09(2) is the correct one. The unattributed $8.50 figure (POL-RD-02 run against the unadjusted 8.2 km optimal, ignoring the closure) does not apply either, because it would penalise the driver for the diversion he was entitled - indeed obliged - to make.

No billing-integrity failure is found. Both gantry charges are matched to the driver's own trace - a fix 0.0 m from the first gantry and 40.25 m from the second, both well inside the 250 m match radius - so POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged and no billing-integrity referral is made against the driver.

The driver cannot convert this into a rider-caused detour that would shut off the ERP correction under POL-RD-09(3). POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider and to identify a place or road specifically enough to act on. The only message naming a route came from the driver ('braddell close today, i take CTE ah', sent 08:12:30) and the rider's single reply 'ok' is an acknowledgement of a decision already announced, with waypoint_hint null on the record. POL-RD-04 is unavailable.

The repeat-deviation uplift and conduct referral in POL-RD-06 are not engaged. The excess is 36.34%, below the 50% material threshold, and assessed on the excess remaining after the POL-RD-03 adjustment it is zero. In any event the driver_profile records 0 deviation flags against 553 completed trips in 90 days, far below the clause's pattern threshold, so there is no basis for a FULL_REFUND uplift or a driver-conduct referral.

The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 100% coverage, 175 fixes at a 10-second interval against an expected 10 seconds, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of POL-RD-07's limbs fires, so no independent corroboration is required and no escalation is triggered. No POL-RD-10 trigger is present: identifiers match, timestamps agree, no cited artifact is missing, and the refund is far below both the $150.00 ceiling and the charged total.

Confidence is 0.90. All the artifacts that carry the deciding facts - the GPS trace, trip record, fare breakdown and traffic advisory - are at full weight (1.0), so the ceiling under POL-GEN-02(2) is 1.0; the small discount reflects only the interpretive choice between the two routes to the correction described above.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
